raw_response:
Useful existing mechanisms for constructing Unicode strings from bounded input

1. Rust String::from_utf8 and from_utf8_lossy
https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/main/library/alloc/src/string.rs
The validated ownership-transfer path and borrow-on-valid lossy path show how a counted byte buffer can become Unicode text without an unconditional full-buffer copy. The opened implementation validates a Vec<u8> and moves that vector into the String on success; its repair interface can borrow already-valid text. This is a useful model for separating ownership, validation, and repair. Reusing arbitrary foreign buffers still requires compatible storage and ownership rules, and repair can allocate. Date status: unknown; the current source was opened, while attempts to retrieve the historical 1.6 material failed.

2. ICU u_strFromUTF8 and u_strFromUTF8WithSub
https://unicode-org.github.io/icu-docs/apidoc/dev/icu4c/ustring_8h.html
These APIs combine explicit input length, caller-provided output capacity, produced length, and strict-or-replacing error policy for bounded bulk Unicode conversion. They offer a concrete C component and a design precedent for decoding an exact byte span, including interior zero bytes. Output storage is necessary when changing representation; sizing first can add a pass. The separate lenient converter should not stand in for a well-formedness guarantee. Date status: unknown because the opened evidence is live development documentation.

3. Foundation NSString initWithBytes:length:encoding:
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsstring/init(bytes:length:encoding:)?language=objc
The counted-buffer initializer is a directly relevant Foundation interface for decoding a specified byte span with a chosen encoding instead of requiring a terminator scan. It is worth examining as an existing interoperation route for Swift. Its zero-copy behavior and bridging cost were not established. Verification is incomplete: the primary search snippet described the initializer, but the HTML required JavaScript and the returned Markdown excerpts exposed only metadata. Date status: unknown.

4. Qt QString explicit-size Unicode constructors
https://doc.qt.io/Archives/qt-4.7/qstring.html
QString::fromUtf8(pointer, size), together with UTF-16 and UCS-4 counterparts, supplies a precedent for using a known input extent instead of scanning for a zero terminator. The archived reference explicitly reserves terminator scanning for the default negative size. Its UTF-8 error behavior can replace or suppress invalid input, so strict rejection would require a separate contract. Convenience constructors can also have different NUL behavior. Date status: unknown; the official 4.7.0 archive was opened, but this run did not verify its calendar publication date.

5. Boost.Locale range-based character-set conversion
https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/develop/libs/locale/doc/html/group__Charset.html
The begin/end overloads of to_utf and from_utf demonstrate encoding-aware conversion of an exact buffer range without sentinel-based extent discovery. A framing parser could select the range before invoking the decoder; that application is an inference from the interface. Conversion policy, output allocation, and backend encoding support still need deliberate choices. Date status: unknown; the develop reference was opened and the attempted 1.60 reference was inaccessible.

6. Java NIO CharsetDecoder incremental decoding
https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/charset/CharsetDecoder.html
Its stateful byte-buffer-to-character-buffer protocol offers an alternative that handles chunk boundaries and explicit end-of-input without first assembling one complete source buffer. The documented protocol reports input/output exhaustion, supports explicit error policies, and finalizes the decoder after the last chunk. This is a useful design precedent for network or file framing. The caller must manage partial sequences, buffer exhaustion, and finalization; string storage is still required. Date status: post-decision evidence, because the search metadata dated this live reference to five months before retrieval in November 2026.

7. UTF8-CPP checked iterator-range conversion
https://github.com/nemtrif/utfcpp
The library's bounded iterator interfaces provide a mechanism for validating and converting byte/code-unit ranges while allowing the caller to choose the output container. The opened example passes begin/end iterators to Unicode conversion routines. Checked conversion and explicit repair policy matter; unchecked entry points do not supply the required safety guarantee. Output capacity should also be managed so that a generic output iterator does not imply repeated reallocations. Date status: unknown; a current README's statement that the project began in 2006 does not establish the age of the exact retrieved interface.

These are candidate components and design precedents, with no claim of deployment or measured usefulness for this problem. Public web search was performed. The unauthenticated grep.app endpoint attempt failed, and subsequent code discovery used public code indexed by web search; that fallback was code-through-web, not successful native code search.
